Messages.Author: Pascal Bertrand
Messages.Body:
As long as they are not marked on the back (or in any other dimension), that's ok.

For instance:
- You can play unaltered Jyhad and Vtes cards, as long as you mix them well enough. That is: if you have Jyhad Parity Shifts in there, you should also have Vtes Parity Shifts, non-Parity Shift Jyhad cards, and non-Parity Shift vtes cards.

- The thickness of the cards must be somewhat coherent. Don't start glueing paper on the cards, it *will* change the feeling in your deck.

- The card must be recognizable, at least from text, title, illustration, or combination of these. Its text must be fully readible. For instance, that  Birds of Paradize wouldn't be a good idea. Most players know you have to tap it to gain 1 of any colour, but some could think you have to pay 2.

- Of course, all cards must be genuine Vtes cards, or official vekn cards printed fllowing the vekn tournament rules. You cannot photocopy (or print a scanned version of) other cards for tournaments.

In the end:
- Use felt-tip pens, markers (or paint markers), not brushes (paint will alter the thickness of the card)
- Leave text readable and understandable (at least the important parts like numbers)

- And post your work here, I'm sure lots of people will enjoy it  I'll post my versions of "re-artworked" cards.

Messages.Author: Juggernaut1981
Messages.Body:
The rules quoted are there to basically mean:

1) Nobody should be able to identify the cards in your library, while they are face down in your library/crypt/uncontrolled.

So, same thickness (or close enough), same backs, no side marks, etc, etc, etc. In effect, you should have no way to tell if the next card in your library is a Parity Shift or a Wake With Evening's Freshness unless you were allowed to look at the card in game.

The earliest editions of the game did not have "Vampire" printed on the back but "Jyhad" printed on the back. Even in some opaque sleeves you can pick them apart. So as a rule, you can't have every copy of a particular card be a Jyhad card and you should have a number of different cards be a Jyhad card (that way you can't be sure what the Jyhad-backed card is on the top of your library/crypt)

2) Cards should still be able to be used/checked by new players.

So the text should be the same, the card format should be similar, the necessary icons should all be present and clearly visible. The fact that you want to have Superman instead of Neo on your Deflections is bleh

Messages.Author: jamesatzephyr
Messages.Body:
> Rémi wrote:
> Thanks Andrew.
>
> > Juggernaut1981 wrote:
> > 1) Nobody should be able to identify the cards in your library, while they are face down in your library/crypt/uncontrolled.
> >
> Is not the reason of using opaque sleeves to avoid this kind of problems. Until a few years ago opaque sleeves were required. Has it changed?
> Anyway, my only one concern is about to change the look of face-up cards.
>
Opaque sleeves prevent you from (easily) identifying the card visually. The problem being addressed is tactile identification.

Take a piece of paper and stick it to a card. Place the card face down. Run your fingers over the back of the card. If it alters the thickness, you will probably be able to tell what card it is. If if alters the thickness in particular places (e.g. you've stuck a piece of paper over only the picture of the vampire on the vampire card), it would be potentially possible to use this to mark your cards. Stick a sequin on the nose of the Sphinx on Dreams of the Sphinx and you would probably be able to easily identify it by touch, even when it's face down, in a sleeve. A wily player would be able to use this information when shuffling a deck or deciding whether to tap The Barrens or whatever else.

If you draw on the card with, say, felt-tip pens or pens like metallic ink, the potential for making the card identifiable by touch is significantly reduced. Not necessarily entirely eliminated, and a judge might still have to intervene in egregious situations, but generally you'd hope not.

Messages.Author: Pascal Bertrand
Messages.Body:
That would be OK, I suppose, but only if the judge approves these cards (agrees to check, and checks that the written cardtext is indeed the up-to-date cardtext). If the judge doesn't have time, then, no.
Which means it's safer to not write on cartext.
